paper_title: MARBLE A Hard Benchmark for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning and Planning
caption: : Search space of the dataset under different configurations.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the growth in the number of possible solutions as a function of the number of missing pieces in the M-Cube dataset, comparing two configurations: “Flip needed” (orange line with circle markers) and “Flip ignored” (blue line with circle markers), both plotted on logarithmic scales. The x-axis, labeled “# Missing pieces,” ranges from 1 to 6 with integer tick marks, while the y-axis, labeled “# Possible solutions,” spans from 10⁰ to 10⁸ with logarithmic spacing. The orange “Flip needed” line starts at approximately 10¹ solutions for 1 missing piece and rises sharply to 10⁸ solutions at 6 missing pieces, passing through points such as ~10² at 2, ~10⁴ at 4, and ~10⁶ at 5. The blue “Flip ignored” line begins at ~10¹ for 1 missing piece and increases more gradually to ~10⁶ at 6 missing pieces, with intermediate values around ~10² at 2, ~10³ at 3, and ~10⁵ at 5. Two red annotations highlight specific points: “CUBE-easy” near (2, 10²) on the blue line and “CUBE” near (6, 10⁸) on the orange line, indicating benchmark configurations. Both lines show exponential growth, with the “Flip needed” condition exhibiting a steeper increase in solution space complexity.
